facts.text: Queen West was laid out as Lot Street in 1793 and became a hub for independent businesses by 1860.
Over a century, Queen West nurtured textiles, fashion, punk music, and graffiti, making it a creative hotspot.
The neighborhood’s architecture, street art, live music venues, and diverse stores keep that history alive today.
Pair an espresso with a freshly baked pastry at Forno Cultura, a third‑generation Italian café and bakery on Queen West.
In May 2023, a 4.5‑year closure of Queen Street between Victoria and Bay Streets began to allow construction of the new Queen station on the Ontario Line.
Early‑works projects for the Ontario Line began in early 2023 at sites including Queen, Corktown, and Osgoode stations, marking the start of the line’s construction.
